name: Use of Hard-coded Credentials
description: Hard-coded credentials occur when authentication information such as passwords, API keys, access tokens, or cryptographic secrets is embedded directly in application source code. Anyone who can access the source code or compiled application may be able to obtain and misuse the credentials.
common_causes: Embedding passwords directly in Python source code
Hard-coding API keys in application files
Storing access tokens directly in source code
Embedding database credentials in configuration code
Using fixed credentials for production services
vulnerable_patterns: Password assigned directly to a string literal
API key assigned directly to a variable
Access token embedded in application source
Database username and password stored directly in Python code
Authentication credentials passed as hard-coded function arguments
Secret values stored in configuration files committed to source control

vulnerable_examples.explanation: A database password is directly embedded in the source code and can be exposed to anyone who gains access to the code.
An API key is stored directly in a Python source file instead of being obtained securely from a secret-management mechanism.
Database credentials are hard-coded directly into the application source.

secure_patterns: Store secrets outside application source code
Use environment variables for appropriate deployment scenarios
Use dedicated secret-management systems for production credentials
Use configuration management that keeps secrets separate from source code
Avoid committing credentials to source-control repositories

secure_examples.explanation: The database password is obtained from an environment variable instead of being embedded directly in source code.
The API key is retrieved from the runtime environment rather than being stored directly in the application source.

detection_indicators: Variable names such as password, api_key, secret, token, or credential contain string literals
Database connection functions receive literal passwords
API clients receive literal API keys or access tokens
Authentication credentials appear directly in Python source
Long high-entropy strings are assigned to security-sensitive variables
Secrets are stored in source files or committed configuration files
Fixed credentials are used for external services
remediation: Remove hard-coded credentials from application source code and rotate credentials that may already have been exposed. Store secrets using appropriate environment configuration or a dedicated secret-management system. Ensure secret-containing files are excluded from source control and establish procedures for credential rotation.

references.title: MITRE CWE-798: Use of Hard-coded Credentials
